content.text:
I submitted **index 20 (Sb fraction 0.88)** as the best composition. It had the highest measured EQE, but that is only 0.00198%, so every composition on this line performs very poorly under 2.4 eV light. This is probably because Zn–Sb oxides have wide band gaps and barely absorb photons at that energy.

I used all 5 EQE measurements:

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | 0.33 | 0.00124 |
| 13 | 0.64 (near ZnSb₂O₆) | 0.00092 |
| 17 | 0.83 | 0.00143 |
| **20** | **0.88** | **0.00198** |
| 25 | 0.93 | 0.00113 |

Index 20 scored higher than both neighbours I measured (indices 17 and 25), which suggests a local peak around Sb ≈ 0.88. But the differences are tiny, and I measured each composition only once. So "best" here may not be much more than measurement noise.

- **Unmeasured areas:** I never measured the Zn-rich end (indices 0–3, near Zn₇Sb₂O₁₂) or the middle of the line (indices 5–12). If the true best composition is in either stretch, I missed it.
- **XRD:** I used 2 of the 5 XRD measurements, on indices 15 and 20. Both showed the same main peak, at Q ≈ 2.79 Å⁻¹. None of the known phases I compared against matched well (similarity scores of 0.25 or less), so I couldn't identify the phase responsible. The XRD didn't change which compositions I measured.
